_comment: Where every sampled sound in the sprite comes from, and the proof. tools/fetch_audio.py downloads each `url` once, checks it against `sha256`, and extracts `member` if it is an archive. static/audio/LICENCES.md is GENERATED from this file, so the credits cannot drift away from the audio the way a hand-written list does. A sound with no entry here is synthesised by tools/make_audio.py and is ours outright.
_licences: CC0 only. Not a stylistic preference: this repository is public and MIT, so an asset carrying an attribution requirement puts an obligation on everyone who clones it, and one carrying a non-commercial clause makes the repository undistributable. CC0 is the only licence with neither. Every entry is checked by tests/test_audio_sources.py.
_gates: Each sound must also survive tools/fetch_audio.py --check: no edge discontinuity, and high-frequency energy in the band its role needs. An archive is not automatically better than synthesis -- three of Kenney's own interface sounds have exactly 0.0% of their energy above 2 kHz, which is the same dullness this work set out to fix.

tap.why: The pack's shortest click. A 50 ms blip under a finger; nobody hears stereo width on one.

flip.why: A card turning over in the pack rip.

scratch.why: 94% of its energy above 2 kHz, which is what a record scratch is. The synthesised one was 9.9%.

buzzer.why: 68% above 2 kHz against the synthesised buzzer's 1.0%, and none of its 510 discontinuities.
